takeaways.t: **France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on 9 Nov that Iran's Revolutionary Guards were responsible for the 11–12 Oct sabotage of refrigeration controllers at about 700 French retail sites;** a five-page government report names the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit, and the Paris prosecutor has requested international arrest warrants. [12, 13]

**US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediate Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, the first trilateral round since February;** Rustem Umerov leads Ukraine's team, Vladimir Medinsky is on Russia's, and European and NATO advisers attend side meetings, and the Kremlin says the talks are trilateral. [14, 15, 16]

**Rep. Thomas Massie offered articles of impeachment against Secretary Hegseth on 9 Nov, and the House floor schedule lists the resolution as an item that may be considered this week;** the same day Hegseth told the Naval War College that the colleges' primary task “must be teaching victory” and ordered 33 changes to them. [17, 18, 19]

**President Trump said on 9 Nov, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, that “Iran militarily is effectively over” while the naval blockade stays;** Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei replied: “STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.” [22]

items.h: Russia and Ukraine send senior teams to Abu Dhabi for US-mediated talks
items.body: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediate talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, the first trilateral round since February. [14, 15] Russia's team includes Vladimir Medinsky, Sergei Ryabkov, Mikhail Galuzin, Igor Kostyukov and General Yury Zhigarlovsky; Ukraine's is led by intelligence chief Rustem Umerov with Kyrylo Budanov and Davyd Arakhamia. [14, 16] European advisers attend side meetings; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov: “What will happen in Abu Dhabi in the coming days is trilateral negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, mediated by the United States.” [26, 16] Secretary of State Rubio on guarantees: “obviously, it has to be something that Russia agrees to as well in order for it to work.” [27]
items.next: Talks continue on 11 Nov; EU leaders take up Europe's place in the process in Ireland on 13 Nov, at Italian Prime Minister Meloni's request. [16]

items.h: Russia sends 317 drones overnight as Ukraine hits Iskander fuel plant near St Petersburg
items.body: The Air Force said Russia launched 317 strike drones and Banderol missiles overnight into 9 Nov, 271 downed or suppressed, with hits at 31 locations. [20] A strike on an Odesa infrastructure facility killed three on 9 Nov, and Centrenergo said the Trypillia power plant was hit again with “extremely serious” consequences. [28, 29] The General Staff said Ukrainian forces damaged three workshops at the Morozov plant near St Petersburg, which makes solid-propellant charges for Iskander-M motors; overnight into 10 Nov a monitoring channel reported explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa. [21, 30] Defence Intelligence published a teardown of the smaller Geran-5 K5-K jet drone. [31]
items.next: US deputy UN envoy Dan Negrea asked both sides on 9 Nov to avoid the “vicious cycle of attacks, retaliation, and death” before the Abu Dhabi round on 10–11 Nov. [32]

items.h: Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ but keeps the naval blockade
items.body: After meeting Qatar's prime minister on 9 Nov, President Trump said “Iran militarily is effectively over” and “We're just keeping it the status quo”, meaning the naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate, but that “we’re locked and loaded”. [22, 33] Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei replied: “FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.” [22] Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Iran's two-day proposal stands and that ships in Hormuz must coordinate with Iranian authorities. [34]
items.next: Trump expects to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov: “We're trying to end the war in Iran.” [35]

items.h: Israel's new Knesset sits as Eisenkot opens talks with ultra-Orthodox parties
items.body: The new Knesset holds its first session and swearing-in on 10 Nov. [36] Israeli media reported that Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Lieberman agreed on 9 Nov to “exhaust all avenues of negotiation with the ultra-Orthodox parties”; United Torah Judaism (7 seats) and Shas (6) set a temporary halt to Haredi conscription as their main condition. [37] Eisenkot's four-party bloc holds 48 of 120 seats and wants to replace Speaker Amir Ohana. [36] In southern Lebanon, the UN said peacekeepers recorded six Israeli airstrikes and 360 artillery trajectories on 5–8 Nov and preparations for a sustained Israeli presence; UNIFIL ends operations on 31 Dec. [38]
items.next: Eisenkot has 28 days from 8 Nov, extendable by 14, to form a government. [37]

items.h: Von der Leyen pledges €60 million for Black Sea surveillance and a security hub
items.body: In Bucharest on 9 Nov, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced about €60 million: €10 million for maritime surveillance and search and rescue, €50 million for a planned Security Hub with Bulgaria, Romania and Türkiye. [39] CMA CGM added a war-risk surcharge of $35 per 20-foot container from 9 Nov for Constanța, Poti, Varna, Burgas and other ports in the region. [40] After a call with Narendra Modi, President Zelensky said: “India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors.” [41] Moldova's foreign minister Mihai Popșoi said European Peace Facility support rose from €7 million in 2021 to €120 million in 2026. [42]
items.next: Von der Leyen meets Prime Minister Rumen Radev in Varna on 10 Nov; Gagauzia elects its governor and 35-seat assembly on 15 Nov. [39, 43]

feature.title: NATO on the Arctic in its own words: Arctic Sentry from launch to Oslo
body: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte told a press conference at NATO headquarters on 11 Feb that Arctic Sentry had been launched “just two hours ago”, bringing NATO and Allied activities in the High North “into one, overarching operational approach to the region”. [44] Initially it brings together exercises such as Denmark's Arctic Endurance and Norway's Cold Response. Rutte called it an enhanced vigilance activity “directly under the authority of the Supreme Allied Commander”, with Allied Command Operations and Joint Force Command Norfolk working with Allied Command Transformation and coordinating with NORAD, US Northern Command and US European Command. [44, 45]

Cold Response ran in March; Rutte said on 11 Jun that more than 30,000 personnel from 14 Allies, including 4,000 US troops, trained above the Arctic Circle. [46] On 6 Jun the NATO Research Vessel Alliance left La Spezia to open Task Force X-Arctic, an 18-month Allied Command Transformation programme to show how networked uncrewed systems can give persistent awareness across the North Atlantic and the Arctic; the Italian Navy crews the ship, the first phase was set off Iceland, and a full-scale demonstration is planned for summer 2027. [45]

At the Ankara Summit on 8 Jul, Rutte traced the activity to his January meeting with President Trump in Davos and named its core as the seven Arctic Allies: the US through NORTHCOM and NORAD, Canada, Iceland, Sweden, Denmark, Finland and Norway. He said the separate US–Denmark–Greenland talks were “up to the three parties”. [47] On 24 Sep General Nick Perry became the first British officer to command JFC Norfolk, which commands Arctic Sentry. [48, 45]

incidents.text: Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on 9 Nov that false claims about the Kraków shooting spread within tens of minutes and were amplified by Russian bots and trolls; his ministry reported more than 2,000 accounts for blocking or moderation in the first 24 hours. [50] NASK's disinformation centre put the false claim that the gunman was a soldier at nearly 18 million reach and a supposed link to the Constitutional Tribunal protests at up to 14 million. [50]

incidents.when: Early 8 Nov (cables cut); a second cable fault in the night to 9 Nov
incidents.text: Federal police say an unknown man cut several signal cables at Köln Messe/Deutz station early on 8 Nov, stopping passenger and freight trains on the line towards Troisdorf and Siegburg/Bonn; Cologne police call it a “Sabotagehandlung” and state-security police are investigating. [51] A second cable fault in the night to 9 Nov knocked out another signal box; whether it was vandalism and linked is under investigation. Trains ran to schedule again early on 9 Nov. About 70 km from Heerlen. [51]

leads.title: France names Iran's Revolutionary Guards behind the October fridge sabotage
leads.teaser: The first government attribution in the refrigeration attacks points to Tehran, not Moscow, and covers only France's 700 sites hit on 11–12 Oct.
rows: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on 9 Nov, at the G7 ministerial in Paris: “Je suis en mesure de confirmer que la responsabilité de cette attaque revient au corps des Gardiens de la révolution de la République islamique d'Iran.” Attackers had taken over Danfoss, Dixell and Copeland refrigeration controllers at about 700 French retail sites in the night of 11–12 Oct, forcing endless defrost cycles with alarms switched off. [12]

France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre (ANSSI, cyber command, DGSE and DGSI) published a five-page report naming the Shahid Kaveh unit of the IRGC Electronic and Cyber Center, citing Farsi artefacts, tooling and infrastructure; it counts at least 15 fires, and says the same hackers targeted Schneider Electric equipment at several small hydroelectric plants. [13]

A3. Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau opened a judicial investigation into the unit's head, his two deputies and others for offences committed “dans le but de servir une puissance étrangère, en l'espèce l'Iran”, and requested international arrest warrants. ANSSI head Vincent Strubel says nothing yet ties the blood-service attack to the same attacker, and the early-November wave in other countries is unattributed. [12, 13]

Iran's ambassador was summoned; Barrot: “Nous prendrons des sanctions à l'échelle européenne contre tous les responsables de cette attaque.” Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul says he has no findings of his own; n-tv reports US officials confirming Iranian hallmarks in the campaign. Iran has not responded officially. [12, 52, 53, 54]
France will seek EU sanctions; no date given. [12]
leads.sw: Only France's October wave is attributed; the early-November attacks that reached Belgian, Dutch and German stores, and the US-base freezer failures the BBC cites, remain open, so baseline requirement 4 (food and water) planning in the JOA has to treat remote refrigeration controllers as an attack surface whoever the actor is.

leads.title: Poland says Russian bots amplified Kraków falsehoods as prosecutors check a Russian lead
leads.teaser: Two days after the market-square shooting, Warsaw is fighting the information aftermath and has not ruled out a hybrid angle to the attack itself.
rows: Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on 9 Nov that false claims appeared “już kilkadziesiąt minut” (“Within tens of minutes, of the attack and were pushed by Russian bots and trolls”); more than 2,000 accounts were reported for blocking in 24 hours. NASK lists claims that the government staged the attack with EU support to cancel the Marsz Niepodległości, that the gunman was a soldier (nearly 18 million reach) and that he was Ukrainian. [50]

A2 for the amplification, named by the minister. On the attack itself, Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said on 9 Nov a Russian hybrid scenario “Nie został wykluczony” (“has not been excluded”), and Eryk Stasielak, head of the National Prosecutor's Office's Kraków department, said “Każdy wątek będziemy badać, również rosyjski” (“We will examine every lead, including the Russian one”). The gunman died in hospital on 9 Nov; prosecutors found four firearms and about 500 rounds and say the motive is still unclear. [55, 56]

Interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka said on 9 Nov the cybercrime bureau CBZC detained six people whose online activity “mogła stanowić potencjalne zagrożenie” (“Could pose a threat, as police watch for copycats”). [57]
Independence Day on Wed 11 Nov brings the Marsz Niepodległości, which one viral false narrative claimed the attack was staged to cancel. [50]
leads.sw: A shooting that turned into a Russian-amplified narrative within tens of minutes is a baseline requirement 6 (civil communications) case; the CIMIC picture for Poland on 11 Nov should carry the NASK narratives alongside the crowd-security posture.

pattern: **Tehran, not Moscow, gets the first attribution:** France names the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit for the October fridge sabotage, after weeks in which Russia was the working suspect. [52, 13]

**The second wave stays open:** ANSSI will not tie the blood-service attack to the same attacker, the November attacks elsewhere are unattributed, and Germany says it has no findings of its own. [12, 52]

**Crises draw information operations:** Poland's minister says Russian bots amplified Kraków falsehoods, and an EU report seen by Reuters says a Russian network exploited France's October riots. [50, 58]
**Rail cables cut near us:** police call the cable cutting at Köln Messe/Deutz on 8 Nov sabotage, about 70 km from Heerlen. [51]
**Summit lockdowns begin:** Dublin's cordon and road closures started on 10 Nov with the Garda drone unit deployed, and Copenhagen bans drones over most of the city until 12 Nov. [59, 60]

europe.h: De Wever's one-on-one budget talks reach Prévot as Justice runs out of money
europe.body: The Prime Minister saw MR deputy prime minister David Clarinval, accompanied by party leader Georges-Louis Bouchez, on 9 Nov and Vooruit's Frank Vandenbroucke at 19:00; Les Engagés' Maxime Prévot follows this morning, and De Wever reports to the King on Mon 16 Nov. [65] The MR holds to the coalition pact's rule of no higher overall tax burden, with “les épaules les plus larges” carrying no more than one ninth of the effort. [65] Separately, the federal justice service told interpreters, forensic doctors and other contractors on 6 Nov that payments are suspended because its 2026 budget for them is exhausted. [66]
europe.sw: SHAPE's host country stays on provisional twelfths until at least 16 Nov, which holds Belgian host-nation-support and defence spending at this year's level.

europe.h: Lithuania weighs renaming Taiwan's Vilnius office before Chinese diplomats visit
europe.body: Delfi reported on 9 Nov that the Foreign Ministry asked the Taiwanese Representative Office on 24 Sep to change its name by 1 Oct, offering a vice-ministerial trip to Taiwan and talks on a double-taxation agreement in return; Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys said the story was “inaccurately reported”. [67] President Gitanas Nausėda said “All matters are coordinated with me” and, asked whether he backs a new name, “We will wait and see.” [68] Chinese diplomats are due in Vilnius on 11–12 Nov, and the government programme aims to restore ambassador-level ties. [67]
europe.sw: Ambassador-level ties with Beijing would put a full Chinese embassy back in a host nation for NATO's forward land forces, a force-protection and host-nation-support factor for staff rotating through Lithuania.

countries.h: Magyar urges NATO-anchored European defence in Berlin before talks with Merz
countries.body: Prime Minister Péter Magyar meets Chancellor Friedrich Merz at the Chancellery today at 11:00 for one-to-one talks, a delegation meeting and a working lunch on Europe, defence, economic cooperation and continued support for Ukraine, with a joint press conference at 13:30. [25] Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, one of four ministers in the delegation, is discussing military, defence-industrial and space cooperation. [69, 70] In a German-language speech at the Konrad Adenauer Foundation on 9 Nov, Magyar said Europe must build real defence capability “a NATO-val, szövetségeseinkkel együtt” (“with NATO and our allies”), and that his government is seeking a legal fix with the Commission this year to stop paying the €1 million daily fine without weakening the southern border. [71]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 3 (uncontrolled movement of people): Magyar keeps the southern-border line while seeking a legal fix in Brussels, and brings his defence minister to Berlin, NATO's logistics hub, for defence-industrial talks.

q.t: Katonai, hadiipari és űripari együttműködésről is egyeztet Berlinben a kormánydelegáció tagjaként Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz.
q.en: As a member of the government delegation, Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi is also holding talks in Berlin on military, defence-industrial and space cooperation.

countries.h: Hungary's €5.4bn EU defence loan pays for SAMP/T and the Záhony bridge
countries.body: 444 reported on 9 Nov, citing a confidential list obtained by Népszabadság, that about €3.45bn of Hungary's €5.4bn loan under the EU's SAFE programme goes to buying and maintaining equipment, among it Lynx infantry fighting vehicles, Leopard tanks, L-39NG trainers, artillery ammunition, Mistral M3 missiles, a SAMP/T air-defence battery, drones and portable counter-drone systems. [72] The list also funds two phases of the M49 road, modernisation of the Záhony bridge, military rail wagons and locomotives, and the EDR digital radio network. [72] The Commission approved the €5.4bn plan, cut from more than €16bn, on 28 Oct and sent it to the Council for approval; no Council date has been announced. [73]
countries.sw: Baseline requirements 7 and 6 (civil transportation, civil communications): EU defence credit for a road, the Záhony border bridge, military rolling stock and the EDR radio network puts Hungary's military-mobility and emergency-radio gaps into a funded plan.

q.t: A tervek között szerepel az M49-es autóút két ütemének megépítése, a záhonyi híd korszerűsítése, katonai vasúti kocsik és mozdonyok beszerzése, valamint az Egységes Digitális Rádiótávközlő Rendszer (EDR) fejlesztése is.
q.en: The plans include building two phases of the M49 road, modernising the Záhony bridge, buying military rail wagons and locomotives, and developing the Unified Digital Radio Communication System (EDR).

countries.h: Slovak army took the defence ministry website offline over a PHP flaw
countries.body: Armed Forces spokesman Štefan Zemanovič told TASR on 9 Nov that the army disconnected the Ministry of Defence website from the internet on 21 Oct after the National Cyber Security Centre warned of two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. [74] The 6th Signal Regiment, which runs the ministry's websites, took it down to prevent loss of data, and the rebuilt site “sa v súčasnosti podrobuje penetračným testom” (“Is now undergoing penetration tests”). [74] The statement answered media reports that the ministry's database of orders and invoices had been deleted: only contracts published since the shutdown are online, and older ones move to the new portal once it is cleared. [74, 75]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 1 (continuity of government): a defence ministry's public portal ran outdated code until the national cyber centre's warning and has been dark for three weeks, with its procurement record offline.

q.t: Ozbrojené sily (OS) SR odpojili 21. októbra webové sídlo Ministerstva obrany (MO) SR od internetu pre kybernetické bezpečnostné riziko.
q.en: On 21 October the Slovak Armed Forces disconnected the Ministry of Defence website from the internet because of a cyber-security risk.

countries.h: Merz ties Germany's yes to the EU budget to Ukraine aid from every member
countries.body: Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote to European Council President António Costa that a joint commitment by all member states to a fair share of Ukraine's funding gap is a precondition for settling other questions with financial effects, dpa and the Financial Times reported on 9 Nov. [23, 24] Kyiv's gap next year is about €70bn, of which the EU intends to cover about €45bn; Slovakia and Bulgaria have announced they will not join new aid, and Czechia and Hungary are counted as reluctant. [23, 24] Leaders take up the gap in Dublin on 12–13 Nov, and Magyar is at the Chancellery today. [23, 24]
countries.sw: EU budget (MFF 2028–2034): Berlin's consent now hangs on Ukraine financing, which puts Hungary's and Slovakia's refusals on the same table as their cohesion and defence money.

q.t: In einem Brief an Ratspräsident Costa, aus dem die Deutsche Presse-Agentur zitiert, droht Merz indirekt mit einer Blockade in anderen Finanzfragen, falls es kein gemeinsames Bekenntnis zur Ukraine-Hilfe gibt.
q.en: In a letter to Council President Costa, quoted by the German Press Agency, Merz indirectly threatens a blockade on other financial questions if there is no joint commitment to aid for Ukraine.

countries.h: Germany pays €6.6bn for the family-held half of tank maker KNDS
countries.body: The federal government pays €6.6bn for the 50% of KNDS held by the owner families through the Wegmann holding, Spiegel reported on 10 Nov, citing parliamentary circles and a confidential finance ministry briefing to the Bundestag. [76] The price is half of an €11.2bn valuation set before the abandoned stock-market listing plus €1bn, and the briefing says a sale to foreign investors, among them Czechia's CSG, “würde die deutschen Sicherheitsinteressen an der Schlüsseltechnologie ›geschützte und gepanzerte Fahrzeuge‹ erheblich gefährden” (“Would seriously endanger German security interests in protected and armoured vehicles”). [76] The purchase contract is due in November and Berlin and Paris intend to sell 10% each later, while the first Boxer tranche of 1,800 vehicles under the Arminius programme is being renegotiated. [76]
countries.sw: Host-nation and reinforcement fleets (Leopard 2, Puma, Boxer) come from KNDS; federal ownership of the German half keeps their intellectual property and output under Berlin's control.

q.t: Der Bund zahlt für den Einstieg beim deutsch-französischen Rüstungskonzern KNDS 6,6 Milliarden Euro.
q.en: The federal government is paying €6.6 billion for its entry into the German-French defence group KNDS.

countries.h: China extends its rare-earth control pause to 10 Jan 2027
countries.body: The commerce ministry and customs administration published Announcement 2026 No. 58 on 9 Nov, in the state's own words: “经批准，自2026年11月11日起至2027年1月10日，商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号，及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号继续暂停实施。” [77] That keeps the October 2025 rare-earth and battery-materials controls suspended from 11 Nov 2026 to 10 Jan 2027 instead of letting them take effect after 10 Nov. [77] Revised export controls on drone-related items, Announcement 2026 No. 49 of 19 Oct, take effect on 18 Nov. [78]
countries.sw: Dual-use supply to the German defence base: the rare-earth cliff moves from 11 Nov to 10 Jan, and the drone-component rules change on 18 Nov.

euregio.h: A nine-minute power cut hits more than 10,000 addresses from Heerlen to Vaals
euregio.body: Power failed at about 06:21 on 9 Nov across an area between roughly Heerlen, Nuth, Valkenburg and Vaals, affecting more than 10,000 addresses for nine minutes; the cause has not been given. [64] Later that morning a cable struck during digging cut power to fewer than 1,000 addresses in 55 postcodes in Kerkrade, most restored by about 10:00, Enexis said. [64]
euregio.fy: Check that a torch and a charged power bank are where everyone in the house can find them in the dark.

euregio.h: Chemelot's largest naphtha cracker trips, lighting a flare seen across the Maas
euregio.body: An abrupt process failure at SABIC's Olefins 4 plant set off full flaring at Chemelot in Geleen from about 17:30 on 9 Nov, with flames metres high and light and noise nuisance; the site gave no end time and said it was doing everything to keep the flaring to a minimum. [79] Residents of Dilsen-Stokkem and Maasmechelen saw the glow, and the company and Dutch Limburg's safety services said it is not a fire. [80]
euregio.fy: A tall flame over Geleen at night is the flare stack; report noise or light nuisance to Chemelot's Milieuklachtenlijn rather than 112.

items.h: Belgium buys NASAMS, radars and Skyranger 30 through the Netherlands
items.body: The Netherlands and Belgium signed agreements in Brussels on 9 Nov under which Belgium buys NASAMS air defence systems, mobile Multi Mission Radars and Skyranger 30 gun platforms through the Netherlands, the same systems the Dutch are buying. [81] Belgian troops have already trained on NASAMS in the Netherlands; Belgium joins the radars' production and international user group, and the Dutch will involve it in testing and in preparing maintenance. [81] Vice Adm. Jan Willem Hartman, commander of the Dutch Materiel and IT Command, signed for the Netherlands; no value or delivery dates were published. [81]
items.sw: Identical Dutch and Belgian air defence fleets give one spares and training chain over the Benelux ports and corridors that carry reinforcements in JFC Brunssum's plans.

items.h: US envoy to NATO calls NATO 3.0 a “factory reset” with no out-of-area role
items.body: Ambassador Matthew Whitaker told Defence24, in an interview published on 9 Nov, that NATO 3.0 “does not get involved in out-of-area operations, and it does not have allies spending less than the amounts required to defend and deter the Alliance.” [82] He said European allies raised spending by $139 billion against 2024 and that all allies must reach the 5% agreed at The Hague: “We cannot have backsliding.” [82] Defence24 notes a meeting of the US-initiated Bergen Group in Kraków on 3 Nov with Poland, Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands, Germany, Norway and Sweden. [82]
items.sw: An alliance confined to Europe puts NATO's planning effort into the regional plans, the north-east sector JFC Brunssum holds among them.

items.h: The Dutch army opens a logistics centre at Soesterberg built with Rhenus
items.body: The Royal Netherlands Army took the Logistiek Centrum Soesterberg into use on 9 Nov, developed with the Rhenus Group as a public-private partnership and part of the build-out of the Soesterberg garrison. [83] Defence Minister Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius said, in Dutch, that with the centre “we invest in the further modernisation of defence logistics”; the ministry and Rhenus say they will keep investing in the chain together. [83]
items.sw: A military logistics hub run with a commercial carrier ties army supply to civilian contracts and staff, a baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation) dependency in host-nation support.

items.h: Ukraine finds 52 US-made parts in a smaller, faster jet Geran-5
items.body: Ukrinform reported on 10 Nov, citing Ukraine's defence intelligence (DIU), that the Geran-5 K5-K used against Ukrainian cities since early autumn is 4 m long against 6.5 m, cruises above 450 km/h at up to 6 km and keeps a 1,000 km range and 90 kg warhead; the sample carried a TBBC-90 thermobaric charge. [31] Its Susanin optical-electronic correlation unit compares a dual-range camera's images with a stored reference on a Chinese Coke Pi microcomputer, and its TRD-200 turbojet is assembled at Alabuga from Chinese parts. [31] The DIU: “Of the 93 electronic components, the largest number – 52 – come from U.S. manufacturers, while China and Switzerland account for 10 each.” [31]
items.sw: A jet Geran above 450 km/h at up to 6 km is the target the NASAMS and Skyranger 30 layers that Belgium and the Netherlands signed for on 9 Nov must reach.

items.h: Kongsberg pitches an uncrewed trawler to hunt Russian submarines for the Royal Navy
items.body: Kongsberg Maritime announced on 9 Nov its Arctic Hunter, a 56 m commercial trawler design with the fish-processing deck replaced by autonomy systems, Thales UK anti-submarine sonar and secure communications, for the Royal Navy's Type 92 uncrewed vessel requirement. [84] A company spokesman said each would patrol unattended for about 60 days, in a flotilla of 10 based “west of the Bear Gap” between Svalbard and Norway, and that ships would be built in the UK. [84, 85] The propeller is to be redesigned to cut noise near the sonar; the Type 92s would work with Type 26 frigates. [84]
items.sw: The Bear Gap is the route Russian submarines take toward the Atlantic reinforcement shipping lanes that JFC Brunssum's north-east plans depend on.

items.h: The US Air Force seeks counter-drone nets for F-35 shelters at Tyndall
items.body: The 325th Contracting Squadron at Tyndall Air Force Base posted market research on 6 Nov for nets around six sunshade shelters, each 630 ft long, 65 ft wide and 30 ft high (about 192 by 20 by 9 m) for up to six F-35As, The War Zone reported on 9 Nov. [86] The nets must be “capable of stopping Group 1 small UAVs from penetrating the structure without compromising the netting”, with tensile strength of at least 200 lb, mesh no wider than 3 inches, quick retraction on the north and south faces and tolerance of 400 °F. [86]
items.sw: A shelter-net specification with mesh and load figures is a template host nations can reuse to harden NATO aircraft shelters, an infrastructure line separate from counter-drone sensor budgets.

items.h: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2, scoring 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0
items.body: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 Nov, one underlying model offered to all users as Fable, with cyber and biology safeguards, and to vetted organisations as Mythos. [87] Anthropic’s own tests put Fable 5.2 at 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 against 45.5% for Opus 5.5 and 42.8% for GPT-6 Astra, and at 64.9% on the RoboDojo Sim two-arm robot test against 29.8% for GPT-6 Astra; 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents formalised Fermat’s Last Theorem in the Lean proof language in 30 hours. [87] Prices fall to $8 per million input and $40 per million output tokens, the UK AI Security Institute and METR tested the model before release, and Fable 5.2 is available now on AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. [87]
items.sw: Fable’s classifiers block exploit and penetration-testing work, so cyber cells would need Mythos access through Anthropic’s verification programme, and today’s CSET report cites a US directive of June this year suspending foreign access to Mythos and Fable; check what allied staff at the headquarters may actually use before building a workflow on it.

items.h: NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 robot model reaches 95% success from five demonstrations
items.body: NVIDIA introduced GR00T 2, an open world action model that predicts future video and robot actions together, with Isaac Lab 3.0 at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin on 9 Nov. [88, 89] On 50 tasks never seen on the target robot it succeeds 40% of the time zero-shot, and five demonstrations per task, under 3 minutes of robot data, raise that to 95% after a 30-minute fine-tune on one RTX 5090 graphics card. [89] It was pretrained on 402,730 hours of egocentric human video, 10,184 hours of handheld-gripper demonstrations and 23,500 hours of robot teleoperation; the smaller GR00T 2 Turbo runs on a Unitree G1 humanoid’s own Jetson Thor at 124 ms per prediction. [89]
items.sw: Robots that learn a task from human video and five demonstrations cut the data cost of automating depot and warehouse work in host-nation-support logistics; ask vendors pitching such systems for scores on the open DexBench and VABAR benchmarks, not demonstrations.

items.h: Meta’s Muse Ember matches Claude Haiku 5.5’s index score at a third of the cost
items.body: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember on 9 Nov, its lightest and cheapest model, built for the work agents repeat all day; Meta’s announcement, as quoted by TechCrunch, puts it as “Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume.” [90] Artificial Analysis scored it 36 on its Intelligence Index at $0.14 per task, the same score as Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.41, and 8 points behind Muse Wonder at about a fiftieth of the cost; list prices are $0.10 per million input and $0.50 per million output tokens. [91] It declined 64% of knowledge questions, which held its hallucination rate to 17.4%, half Haiku 5.5’s, and it is offered through Meta’s first-party API and Muse Code. [91]
items.sw: A cheap model that declines rather than invents suits high-volume staff chores such as extracting fields from host-nation documents or sorting incoming reports, where a wrong answer costs more than a blank; check data-handling terms first, since it runs on Meta’s own API.

cards.n: Massie's resolution is on the House floor schedule; NOS and tagesschau say a vote could come by midweek. [17, 92, 18]
Hegseth's order of 9 Nov for senior service colleges: Warfighter Chairs, graded wargames, no tenure for new civilian faculty. [19, 93]
Fielded under the 2025 Drone Dominance memo; the 12th division starts receiving them in December. [94]
Lt. Gen. Admiral is still awaiting a Senate floor vote on the Executive Calendar of 10 Nov. [95]

words.role: Secretary of Defense (styled Secretary of War)
words.where: U.S. Naval War College, Spruance Hall, Newport
words.quote: Victory: Our ultimate screening criteria. It is the unsparing standard against which every regulation, every doctrine, every budget dollar, and every academic syllabus should be judged.
words.context: He spoke to nearly 700 students, faculty and staff as he issued a memo with 33 requirements for the senior service colleges; Military Times also quotes him: “The American people do not entrust their blood, their treasure, or their sons and daughters in our armed forces to lose or to fight to a draw.” [19, 93]

dod.h: Hegseth orders 33 changes to the senior service colleges in a Newport speech
dod.body: Secretary Hegseth told nearly 700 students, faculty and staff at the U.S. Naval War College on 9 Nov that the colleges' primary task “must be teaching victory”, and issued a memo the same day with 33 implementation requirements from a review led since March by Under Secretary for Personnel and Readiness Anthony Tata. [19] The memo creates “Warfighter Chair” posts for O-5 and O-6 commanders fresh from operational deployments, replaces seminar grading with standardised end-of-course wargames and exams, and moves newly hired civilian faculty from tenure to three-year performance contracts. [19] Military Times reports that the colleges must “ensure that the majority of full-time faculty possess direct military experience and defense experience” and that the directives take effect immediately. [93]
dod.sw: Senior service college seats and the new Warfighter Chair posts are a common next assignment for US field-grade officers leaving NATO staff tours, and the graded wargame now replaces the seminar paper as the measure.

dod.h: US bases at Lakenheath and Mildenhall go to enhanced force protection
dod.body: A US official told The War Zone on 9 Nov: “Enhanced force protection measures are in effect across RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall,” and declined to discuss the measures for operational security reasons. [96] A flight-tracking account reported KC-135 tankers moving from Mildenhall to Spangdahlem in Germany or Prestwick and CV-22Bs to Lakenheath the same day, and Lakenheath asked the community to report drones; US Air Forces in Europe (USAFE) would not comment on asset movements. [96] The War Zone could not establish a link to the inquiry into whether Iran was behind the September incident at RAF Fairford. [96]
dod.sw: EUCOM's 3 Nov security campaign already covers Brunssum staff and families; this is the first base-level rise in protection reported since, and it moved US tankers onto a German base.

news.h: The Army fields launched effects to 11 of its 12 divisions
news.body: Lt. Col. Hunter Gray, product manager for launched effects, told reporters on 5 Nov that 11 of 12 division headquarters and every multi-domain task force (MDTF) have received the drones, with the 12th division to start in December, Breaking Defense reported on 9 Nov. [94] Griffon Aerospace supplies the majority, mostly long-range systems including its Outlaw drone, at “hundreds of systems per month”; Gray: “From the time that we identified the need to scale to the time that the first tranche of systems was delivered was about three weeks.” [94] Payloads cover reconnaissance, electronic warfare and strike; the Army did not name the divisions or give a total. [94]
news.sw: Every multi-domain task force, USAREUR-AF's included, now holds launched effects, a long-range sensing and strike layer for the exercises JFC Brunssum plans with US Army units in Europe.

congress.h: Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution reaches the House floor schedule
congress.body: Rep. Thomas Massie offered his resolution on 9 Nov as the House met for the first time since the midterms, and the weekly floor schedule added “Impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, for high crimes and misdemeanors” as an item that may be considered, with no number yet. [17, 18] The 34-page text opens with Article I, waging war in contravention of section 2(c) of the War Powers Resolution of 1973, over hostilities against Iran from 28 Feb 2026; tagesschau counts eight articles, Yemen and Venezuela among them. [97, 92] NOS reports a vote could come on Wednesday, and Hegseth has called a press conference for today, his first in more than half a year; President Trump said he still backs him. [92, 18]
congress.sw: The vote falls while the Europe posture options sit with the Secretary, the official who signs the decision JFC Brunssum plans against.

congress.h: Admiral's USAREUR-AF nomination is still on the Senate calendar as the lame duck opens
congress.body: The Senate Executive Calendar for 10 Nov still lists Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral (PN1188) as Calendar No. 924, reported by the Armed Services Committee on 23 Sep without a floor vote. [95] Lt. Gen. David Miller Jr.'s Space Command nomination (PN1413) is not on the calendar, so it has not been reported out of committee. [95] The Senate met on 9 Nov and meets again today at 12:00 EST. [98]
congress.sw: Admiral would also take NATO's Allied Land Command, empty since 2 Jul, the land component headquarters JFC Brunssum calls on.

items.h: TRICARE's 2027 co-pays rise about 4%; active-duty families still pay no fees
items.body: Military Times reported on 9 Nov that 2027 co-payments rise about 4%, $1 to $3 per outpatient visit; an emergency-room visit for a Group A active-duty family in TRICARE Select goes from $103 to $107, and the Group B Select deductible for families of E-5 and above rises $14 to $411. [99] Active-duty families pay no enrollment fees and pharmacy costs do not change; changes made in open season (to 8 Dec, FEDVIP and FSAFEDS to 14 Dec) take effect 1 Jan. [99] The IRS release list still ends at IR-2026-134 of 6 Nov with no 2027 retirement-plan limits. [100]
items.fy: Check the family's plan and the FSAFEDS dependent-care and health-care accounts before 8 and 14 Dec; hold any TSP change until the IRS publishes the 2027 limit.
items.sw: US families at Brunssum on Select pay the new deductibles and cost-shares from 1 Jan; Prime stays free for active-duty families who follow its referral rules.

2027 tax year, retiree COLA and TRICARE cost changes take effect

research.org: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), Georgetown University
research.title: Coalition Operations: The Untapped Role of AI in Military Decision-Making
research.authors: Emelia Probasco, Sophie Mayo, Lauren Kahn
summary: The authors ask whether AI-enabled decision support systems (AI-DSS), “software platforms that ingest, analyze, visualize, and share vast and disparate data”, can ease the old frictions of coalition warfare: incompatible networks, conflicting classification rules and national caveats tracked in “enormous spreadsheets”. [102] They examine four uses, a common operational picture, coalition targeting, foreign disclosure and translation, with the Maven Smart System (MSS) as the exemplar, and find real advantages in each, but conclude that “political will and bureaucratic change remain critical hurdles.” [102] Large language models could draft sanitised intelligence reports where disclosure guidance is simple, and help officers who face heavy penalties for over-release but few for over-classification and so “typically err on the side of over-sanitizing”. [101, 102]

The obstacles are political limits on sharing, unequal technical and security standards and distrust of partners and of the technology, now joined by backlash against US vendors and a push for “sovereign AI”. [102] Cross-domain solutions, which pass data from classified US networks to the Mission Partner Network on which NATO Maven runs, were named by US European Command and NATO representatives as “a leading bottleneck” to wider allied use. [102] NATO is the exception they hold up: accreditation of MSS on its networks took six months to an interim approval against up to 18 months on US networks, which the authors, offering hypotheses, put down to more than 75 years of sharing agreements, live demonstrations and a sharper sense of threat. [102]
findings: **Spread:** MSS went from an experiment at one unit to an estimated 50,000 licences across the US Department of War between 2021 and early 2026, a figure from author interviews that the authors say has not been independently verified. [102]

**NATO speed:** SHAPE called its March 2025 purchase “the most expeditious in NATO’s history, taking only six months from outlining the requirement to acquiring the system”; Task Force Maven reports $6 million in annual savings from its use in support of NATO training requirements. [102]

**Allied uptake:** at least ten NATO countries were reportedly in talks over MSS or a related Palantir product by October 2025; the UK signed for up to £750 million over five years, Germany and Switzerland rejected Palantir, and France wants a sovereign equivalent in operation in late 2027. [102]
**The Netherlands:** committed to trying MSS while officials voiced scepticism, and public pushback led the largest Dutch pension fund to divest its Palantir shares. [102]

**Kosovo benchmark:** in Operation Allied Force 64% of targets needed approval above the commanding general and more than 150 were still awaiting approval when the operation ended, the validation load AI review of targeting packages is meant to lighten. [102]

**Compute consensus:** 22 nations signed a letter of intent for NATO’s Allied software for Cloud and Edge (ACE) programme in 2024 but only 12 committed in 2025; contracts are expected in late 2026 and full rollout is targeted for 2030. [102]
research.method: A qualitative policy analysis: a review of open sources on AI-DSS, four coalition use cases built around MSS as the exemplar, historical cases (Afghanistan, Kosovo, the 2004 tsunami response) and author interviews and conversations with Task Force Maven at SHAPE and with NATO and US military members, plus one test of a disclosure task run with Anthropic’s Claude. It measures no operational effect; several figures (the 50,000 licences, the $6 million in savings) rest on interviews or on the programme’s own reporting; the authors say MSS is the system they know best; and the balance between automation and human judgment is left out of scope. [102]
research.sw: For Brunssum: the report’s call for standard data-use agreements with NGOs and international organisations, and its warning that raw feeds risk mixing humanitarian data with military data, lands on J9 civil-military work; ask which civil and NGO data may enter the headquarters’ NATO Maven picture, under what agreement, and whether the cross-domain link is the bottleneck here too.

research.org: Kiel Institute for the World Economy
research.title: How much aid has Germany given to Ukraine? (Kiel Policy Brief No. 217)
research.authors: Federico Mellace, Taro Nishikawa, Christoph Trebesch, Nathanael Frey, Ettore Goffi
summary: The Ukraine Support Tracker team takes apart the EUR 100 billion that the German government reports as support for Ukraine and finds that it measures something else: “the (potential) cost of the war against Ukraine for the German federal budget.” [104] Rebuilding the figure line by line from federal budget documents and parliamentary answers, they put Germany’s bilateral aid between EUR 31 billion, what the Tracker can verify item by item, and EUR 42 billion, the government’s own figures restricted to aid directed to Ukraine. [104] About EUR 35.9 billion of the headline was spent in Germany, mostly on Bürgergeld benefits for Ukrainian refugees, and EUR 22 billion is military aid promised for future years. [104, 105] Their verdict is that Germany’s aid is “sizeable but not exceptional”, and they ask Berlin to report aid to Ukraine apart from spending at home, with values and dates. [103, 104]
findings: **Verified bilateral aid:** EUR 30.8 billion from the start of the war to 31 Aug 2026, 0.86% of 2021 GDP, of which EUR 25.0 billion (81%) is military. [104]

**Inside the EUR 100.9 billion:** EUR 34.6 billion refugee support in Germany, EUR 1.3 billion export guarantees, up to EUR 7.4 billion civilian aid that can reach Ukraine, about EUR 34.2 billion military aid paid or budgeted to the end of 2026 and EUR 22.0 billion falling due from 2027. [104]

**Trend:** allocations fell to EUR 4.4 billion in 2024 and more than doubled to EUR 9.4 billion in 2025; Germany averaged EUR 5.3 billion a year in 2022–2024 and EUR 8.9 billion a year since January 2025, first among 12 large donors in the later period. [104]

**Ranking:** second-largest bilateral donor after the US (EUR 115.4 billion) but twelfth as a share of GDP; adding EUR 22.7 billion of attributed EU-level aid, mostly loans, gives EUR 53.5 billion (1.49% of GDP) and tenth place. [104]

**At home:** the federal top-up to the pension system came to almost EUR 600 billion over 2022–2026, more than ten times bilateral aid, and the 2022/23 “Doppelwumms” energy relief cost about EUR 51 billion. [104]

**Transparency:** only 22% of German aid items in the Tracker carry a value from the source, against 70% on average and 97% for Sweden, Denmark and Australia; Germany scores 4.08 on the transparency index, fifteenth of 42 donors. [104]
research.method: Two sources set side by side: the Ukraine Support Tracker (Release 31, to 31 Aug 2026), which counts only aid that can be dated, valued and traced to a public source, and the government’s August 2026 overview (figures to 30 Jun 2026), reconstructed from federal budget titles and parliamentary questions; EU-level aid is attributed to Germany by its share of the EU budget and EIB capital. The brief cannot split refugee spending further, cannot say how much of the 2026 military appropriation has been paid out, cannot fill Germany’s contributions to the European Peace Facility, and could not trace EUR 1.3 billion of the government’s military total, in part because Berlin stopped publishing item lists of deliveries after April 2025. [104]
research.sw: Germany now gives more new bilateral aid to Ukraine than any other donor, so which German figure is quoted in NATO and EU burden-sharing debates, EUR 31 billion, EUR 42 billion or EUR 100 billion, changes how allies compare.

research.org: Global Carbon Project (Earth System Science Data, Copernicus Publications)
research.title: Global Carbon Budget 2026
research.authors: Pierre Friedlingstein, Michael O’Sullivan, Robbie M. Andrew and 141 co-authors
summary: The 21st annual budget combines energy statistics, land-use bookkeeping models, ocean and land models and atmospheric measurements into the five components of the global carbon budget. [106, 107] Its preliminary estimate for 2026 is that fossil CO2 emissions fall 0.4% (range -1.5% to +0.6%) to 38.2 GtCO2, with oil down 1.9% and gas down 0.3%, partly offset by coal up 0.6%. [106] The team’s release calls the oil drop “likely a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict”, and Pierre Friedlingstein says “a reduction driven partly by geopolitical shocks is not a sustainable climate solution.” [107] Land-use emissions rise, so total emissions reach a projected 43.3 GtCO2, and the remaining budget for a 50% chance of holding warming to 1.5°C is “nearly exhausted”: 150 GtCO2 from the start of 2027, less than four years at 2026 levels. [106]
findings: **Oil:** -1.9% globally in 2026 (range -2.6% to -1.2%), with China’s oil emissions -4.6% and the EU’s -1.8%; the EU total falls to about 2.4 GtCO2. [106]
**Decoupling:** fossil emissions fell in 40 countries with growing GDP over 2016–2025, against 22 in 2006–2015; together they emit 26% of world fossil CO2. [106]
**Slower growth:** total CO2 emissions grew 0.3% a year over 2016–2025 against 1.7% a year over 2006–2015; the 2025 total was 42.8 GtCO2. [106]

**Atmosphere and sinks:** CO2 is set to reach 427.7 ppm in 2026; the land sink rebounded to 3.6 GtC in 2025 after the 2023–24 El Niño, and novel carbon removal offsets less than 30 minutes of annual fossil emissions. [106, 107]
**Other budgets:** 510 GtCO2 remain for 1.7°C (12 years at current rates) and 1,035 GtCO2 for 2°C (24 years). [106]
research.method: A living-data synthesis by more than 140 scientists: fossil emissions from energy and cement statistics, land-use emissions from three bookkeeping models, the atmospheric growth rate from surface stations, and ocean and land sinks from models and observation-based products, with uncertainties at ±1σ. [106, 107] The 2026 figures are projections from partial-year data (for the EU, Eurostat monthly energy data through July or August) and the range includes a small rise; land-use estimates carry large uncertainty; the paper is a preprint in open review at Earth System Science Data, and the link between the oil fall and the Iran conflict is drawn in the team’s release, not in the preprint text. [106, 107]
research.sw: Part of this year’s fall in oil emissions comes from the Iran war’s energy shock rather than from structural change, so for European energy and climate planning the 2026 dip measures disruption as much as transition.

philosophy.year: c. 5th–4th century BCE (compiled by first- and second-generation disciples, on the traditional account)
philosophy.tradition: Non-Western (Confucius, Zhuangzi, Nagarjuna, al-Farabi, Ibn Khaldun)
philosophy.quote: “The Master said, ‘The requisites of government are that there be sufficiency of food, sufficiency of military equipment, and the confidence of the people in their ruler.’ … The Master answered, ‘Part with the food. From of old, death has been the lot of all men; but if the people have no faith in their rulers, there is no standing for the state.’”
philosophy.translation: James Legge, Confucian Analects, from The Chinese Classics (Project Gutenberg eBook 3330); the ellipsis marks Zigong’s two questions and the first answer, “The military equipment.” [108] The Chinese: 「足食，足兵，民信之矣。」…「去食。自古皆有死，民無信不立。」 [109]
philosophy.gloss: The chapter is an argument by forced choice: Zigong (Legge’s Tsze-kung) makes Confucius drop the three requisites of government one at a time, weapons first and then food, so that the order of sacrifice shows what a state finally rests on. [108] Food goes before trust because death comes to everyone in any case, whereas a people without faith in its rulers leaves no state at all; trust is not one asset among three but the condition under which food and arms can be used. [108] The chapter sits in Book XII, a run of dialogues on humaneness and government that goes on to the image of the ruler’s virtue as wind bending grass (12.19), and Mark Csikszentmihalyi’s Stanford Encyclopedia entry reads it as the furthest reach of a virtue that runs through the Analects: “trustworthiness was superior to either food or weapons”. [110] The strongest objection is Han Fei’s, as Yuri Pines reconstructs it: moral suasion held only in a remote age when “the people were few whereas goods were plenty”, and once people multiplied and “provisions are scanty; hence the people compete”, so that, in Pines’s words, “moral norms are no longer sufficient to control social contention; it can be quelled only through coercion.” [111] On that view Confucius has the order backwards, since in scarcity obedience comes from the ruler’s positional power and from rewards and punishments, not from the people’s faith. [111]
philosophy.why: If a host nation under strain could keep only two of food supply, defence stocks and public trust in its government, which would its civil preparedness plan give up first, and does our baseline-requirements assessment ever ask?

deep.title: “The era of subsidised defence”: Hegseth's week as RIA tells it
body: At 06:03 Moscow time on 10 Nov, RIA Novosti, Russia's state news agency, ran Hegseth's Newport speech as “Hegseth: the US is stopping subsidising Europe's defence”. It quoted him, in Russian: “The principles that guided American state policy for 80 years have been revised. For example, we are changing the nature of our relations with Europe: the era of subsidised defence is coming to an end.” It added that European allies must carry the main share of defence in their region and that Trump had accused NATO members of shifting the burden onto American taxpayers. [112] The Naval War College's and Military Times' accounts of the same speech lead with the 33-point education memo and do not carry the Europe line. [19, 93]

At 00:41 the same night RIA reported Trump's defence of Hegseth, citing Reuters, in its Russian rendering: “Well, he won two wars. I don't know how you can impeach him,” and “What about impeaching the people responsible for Vietnam, Afghanistan, Iraq and everything else, where we fought endlessly and nothing happened?” It described Massie's resolution as accusing Hegseth of malfeasance in office and exceeding his authority. [113]

At 06:53 RIA carried, from the i Paper, the case of a British corporal sentenced to 10 months' military detention and demoted to lance corporal after hackers reached private photographs on his phone during a NATO exercise in Estonia and demanded £350. RIA quoted the paper that British troops abroad must remove SIM cards, switch off geolocation and use only a private internal network, and that the source of the hack was not identified. [114] All three items rest on US and British sources: the Secretary's own words, Reuters and a British newspaper.

items.h: The Kamer resumes the tax plan today as a box 3 majority comes into view
items.body: The Tweede Kamer debates the “Pakket Belastingplan 2027 (voortzetting)” from 16:15 to 23:00 today and votes on Thursday. [133, 134] In Monday's box 3 debate JA21 and SGP spoke favourably of moving to a tax on realised gains, putting a majority in view for the minority cabinet, although the change yields an estimated €22 billion less to 2040 and leaves a gap of up to €17.6 billion after 2031. [134] PVV MP Vlottes called the funding “fantoomdekking” and kept his vote open, and members want Finance Minister Heinen, in Brussels on Monday, to answer before deciding. [134] Prime Minister Jetten has dropped his trip to COP31 to stay for the vote. [135]
items.fy: If you hold Dutch savings or investments, the box 3 change starts in 2028 at the earliest and possibly 2029; hold off on any moves until the Senate votes.

items.h: Water-board tax rises about €35 to €535 for a typical owner-occupier in 2027
items.body: The Union of Water Boards said on 9 Nov that the 21 boards' proposals put next year's bill for a household in an owner-occupied home valued at €370,000 at about €535, €35 more, and a single tenant's at about €228, up €15; boards set exact rates in the coming weeks and assessments arrive around 1 Mar. [136] Finance board member Floor Wissing-Kunst said the boards are also preparing for prolonged power outages and attacks on their digital systems. [136]
items.fy: Budget €15 to €35 more for next spring's water-board bill, depending on whether you rent or own.

otd.title: On this day · 10 November 1918
otd.body: On 10 November 1918 the deposed German Emperor Wilhelm II reported to the Dutch checkpoint at Eijsden and applied for political asylum in the neutral Netherlands; the Dutch government had been told he was coming and admitted him. [145] Chancellor Max von Baden had announced the Kaiser's abdication the day before, while Wilhelm sat at the army's headquarters in Spa, and he was forced into exile the next morning; a Dutch student photographed him and his entourage on the Eijsden station platform, waiting for the royal train. [146] Film shot that day shows officers walking the platform while approval for the crossing was pending; Germany signed the armistice on 11 November. [147] He lived first at Amerongen Castle and from 1920 at Doorn, where he died in 1941. [145]

culture.title: Elfde van de Elfde: fools' day opens the season
culture.body: Wednesday is the Elfde van de Elfde, when the carnival season begins; on this “gekkendag”, fools' day, the Raad van Elf chooses the year's Prins Carnaval. [8] The voorseizoen that follows builds towards the prince's takeover on the first day of carnival, with sessions that mock the civic authorities and often a song picked as that year's anthem. [8] In Limburg a prince reigns for one season only, flanked by his Raad van Elf, while in Brabant the same figure can serve for years. [8] Hoensbroek holds its Leedjeskonkoer, the carnival song contest, at the castle on Wednesday, and Heerlen starts a night early with Aod òp Nuj tonight. [10, 5]

items.kop: Gesprekken over Oekraïne in Abu Dhabi
items.nl: Vandaag en morgen praten Rusland en Oekraïne met elkaar in Abu Dhabi. Twee Amerikaanse gezanten, Jared Kushner en Steve Witkoff, leiden de gesprekken. Het is de eerste keer sinds februari dat de drie landen samen aan tafel zitten. Adviseurs uit Europa en van de NAVO zijn er ook bij.
items.en: Today and tomorrow Russia and Ukraine talk to each other in Abu Dhabi. Two American envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, lead the talks. It is the first time since February that the three countries sit at one table. Advisers from Europe and NATO are there too.
woorden: to take part in the talks

items.kop: Zware nacht van drones boven Oekraïne
items.nl: Rusland viel Oekraïne in de nacht van zaterdag op zondag aan met 317 drones en raketten. Oekraïne zegt dat het er 271 heeft neergehaald of gestoord. Oekraïne viel zelf een fabriek bij Sint-Petersburg aan. Die fabriek maakt brandstof voor Iskander-raketten.
items.en: Russia attacked Ukraine in the night from Saturday to Sunday with 317 drones and missiles. Ukraine says it shot down or jammed 271 of them. Ukraine itself attacked a factory near St Petersburg. That factory makes propellant for Iskander missiles.

items.kop: Frankrijk wijst naar Iran na sabotage in winkels
items.nl: In oktober gingen in ongeveer 700 Franse winkels de koelingen kapot door een cyberaanval. De Franse minister van Buitenlandse Zaken zegt nu dat de Iraanse Revolutionaire Garde dit heeft gedaan. Een rapport van de regering noemt de eenheid Shahid Kaveh. De officier van justitie in Parijs vraagt om internationale arrestatiebevelen.
items.en: In October the refrigeration in about 700 French shops broke down because of a cyberattack. The French foreign minister now says Iran's Revolutionary Guards did this. A government report names the Shahid Kaveh unit. The Paris prosecutor is asking for international arrest warrants.

items.kop: Merz koppelt de EU-begroting aan steun voor Oekraïne
items.nl: Duitsland wil de nieuwe EU-begroting voor 2028 tot 2034 alleen goedkeuren als alle landen meebetalen aan Oekraïne. Dat melden persbureau dpa en de Financial Times. Vandaag om 11.00 uur ontvangt bondskanselier Merz de Hongaarse premier Magyar in Berlijn. Magyar neemt vier ministers mee.
items.en: Germany will only approve the new EU budget for 2028 to 2034 if all countries help pay for Ukraine. The news agency dpa and the Financial Times report this. Today at 11:00 Chancellor Merz receives the Hungarian prime minister Magyar in Berlin. Magyar brings four ministers.

items.kop: Tweede Kamer praat verder over het belastingplan
items.nl: De Tweede Kamer bespreekt vandaag van 16.15 tot 23.00 uur het Belastingplan 2027. Donderdag stemt de Kamer. Er lijkt een meerderheid te komen voor een nieuwe manier van belasting op sparen en beleggen. Ook de waterschapsbelasting gaat omhoog: ongeveer 35 euro meer voor een gezin met een koophuis.
items.en: The House of Representatives discusses the 2027 tax plan today from 16:15 to 23:00. On Thursday the House votes. A majority seems to be forming for a new way of taxing savings and investments. The water-board tax also goes up: about 35 euros more for a family in an owner-occupied home.

items.kop: Korte stroomstoring tussen Heerlen en Vaals
items.nl: Zondagochtend om 6.21 uur viel de stroom uit tussen Heerlen, Nuth, Valkenburg en Vaals. Meer dan 10.000 adressen zaten negen minuten zonder stroom. De oorzaak is nog niet bekend. Zondagavond viel bij Chemelot in Geleen de grootste fabriek uit. Daardoor was een grote vlam te zien, tot in België.
items.en: On Sunday morning at 06:21 the power failed between Heerlen, Nuth, Valkenburg and Vaals. More than 10,000 addresses were without power for nine minutes. The cause is not yet known. On Sunday evening the largest plant at Chemelot in Geleen tripped. That produced a large flame, visible as far as Belgium.
